answer:
A confounder $A\leftarrow C\rightarrow B$ creates a backdoor association; adjusting for suitable pre-treatment common causes can block it. A mediator $A\rightarrow M\rightarrow B$ carries part of a causal effect; conditioning on it generally changes the target from total effect toward a direct-effect question. A collider $A\rightarrow Z\leftarrow B$ blocks that path until conditioning on it or its descendant opens an association. [1](https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook)

For example, selection based on either strong coding or strong research makes one strength compensate for the other among selected applicants. Adjustment is therefore determined by the causal graph and estimand, not by including every predictive feature. Verify temporal ordering and assumptions; observational associations alone do not identify the graph or eliminate unmeasured confounding. Conditioning can remove bias on one path while creating it on another.

![Conditioning has different consequences for common causes, mediators, and colliders.](/answer-diagrams/causal.svg)
